programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
programme.sub-title: An Overview of Democracy in America
programme.desc: The course begins with a brief overview of Tocqueville's masterwork; written to educate the French about democracy; it is originally published as two separate volumes, released five years apart.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
programme.desc: William R. Cook introduces the young French nobleman, trained as a lawyer; his most famous book is only one achievement in a life marked by several; service as France's foreign minister; a history of the French Revolution regarded as a classic.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
programme.desc: Tocqueville rarely describes specific events or conversations; his letters and journals allow one to follow him on his trip; getting an excellent feel for the experiences he and his colleague, Gustave de Beaumont, have in America.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
programme.desc: This lecture considers the meaning and implications of what Tocqueville introduces in the first paragraph of "Democracy in America"; the foundation of the democratic enterprise; the concept he calls equality of conditions.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
programme.desc: The key historical forces that characterize the Gilded Age and the Progressive Era; the competing ideals that define these eras; the US in 1865; the extraordinary social, political and economic changes unleashed by the devastation of the Civil War.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
programme.desc: The Reconstruction era following the Civil War; governmental policies and legislation enacted to safeguard the welfare of former slaves and average citizens; these policies are progressively dismantled, the South comes under the rule of the whites.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
programme.sub-title: Buffalo Bill Cody and the Myth of the West
programme.desc: The story of the conquest of the American West; key myths surrounding the West and how it is settled; the motives and realities of westward migration; the components of the western economy; the conflicts with Native Americans that lead to violence.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
programme.desc: America rises from a developing nation status in 1865 to become a great industrial power by 1900; the unfolding of the American industrial revolution; the advent of big business in the railroad, steel and oil industries; consumerism and advertising.

programme.title: Understanding the World's Greatest Structures: Science and Innovation from Antiquity to Modernity
programme.sub-title: Learning to See and Understand Structure
programme.desc: How ideas for buildings, bridges and towers transform from sketches to concrete reality; three essential qualities that make a structure great; the difference between seeing a structure and actually understanding it.

programme.title: Understanding the World's Greatest Structures: Science and Innovation from Antiquity to Modernity
programme.sub-title: The Science of Structure - Forces in Balance
programme.desc: Exploring how two types of external forces act on structures such as the Chouteau Bridge in Kansas City; learning how the forces are related to equilibrium, the most important concept in the field of engineering mechanics.

programme.title: Understanding the World's Greatest Structures: Science and Innovation from Antiquity to Modernity
programme.desc: Using the Simple Tension Test as a gateway to understanding the concepts of internal force, stress and strength; seeing the concepts at work in structures such as San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge and Athens's Olympic Velodrome.

programme.title: Understanding the World's Greatest Structures: Science and Innovation from Antiquity to Modernity
programme.sub-title: From Wood to Steel - Properties of Materials
programme.desc: How materials profoundly influence the form, function and structure of great buildings, bridges and towers; using steel as a benchmark; comparing the structural properties of wood, masonry, concrete and iron; seeing the materials at work.

programme.title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
programme.desc: The experiences of Julia, the daughter of Caesar Augustus; a window into the way many pre-modern societies sought to control morality; Julia's life of thwarted potential; understanding what women had to overcome to make a mark on history.

programme.title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
programme.sub-title: Herodias Has John the Baptist Beheaded
programme.desc: The portrayal of the John the Baptist's death as the whim of the young femme fatale Salome; why the truth is much more complicated; the story of Salome's mother, Herodias; how Herodias's hunger for power and recognition left her exiled and forgotten.

programme.title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
programme.sub-title: The Trung Sisters of Vietnam Fight the Han
programme.desc: China under the Han Dynasty; how imperial expansion threatened the matriarchal culture of Vietnam; the Trung sisters; leading tribal armies against the invaders; how the Trung sisters' story has become a touchstone of Vietnamese culture.

programme.title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
programme.desc: The end of Iron Age Britain and the birth of Roman Britain; the valiant but thwarted rebellion of the Celtic warrior queen, Boudicca; how Boudicca was motivated by personal tragedy; the revival of Boudicca's legacy by Queen Victoria.

programme.title: England, the 1960s, and the Triumph of the Beatles
programme.sub-title: The Magical Mystery of the Beatles
programme.desc: What happens between September 1963 and February 1964 to launch the Beatles toward international stardom; discovering some of the major social and sonic factors at work in the transformation of these young musicians into a pop culture hurricane.

programme.title: England, the 1960s, and the Triumph of the Beatles
programme.desc: The Beatles are a product of the many worlds contained within 1950s and 1960s Liverpool; how the band soaks up this post-industrial and culturally vibrant scene; how they store ideas and impressions that turn up in some of their early tunes.

programme.title: England, the 1960s, and the Triumph of the Beatles
programme.sub-title: Finding the Beat in the Beatles
programme.desc: The "beat" in the Beatles is about more than just the music; exploring the Bohemian fringe known as the beatniks; following John, Paul and George as they search for the right drummer; the importance of the Beatles' apprenticeship in Hamburg.

programme.title: England, the 1960s, and the Triumph of the Beatles
programme.sub-title: Nowhere Men: The Dark Side of the Beatles
programme.desc: Professor Shelden reveals some of the less flattering characteristics of the Beatles; chief among these is anger, both as a problem for John Lennon and as an outlet for creativity best seen in one of the Beatles' early successes, "Help!".

programme.desc: Smithsonian artifacts tell the story of the quest for religious freedom in America; a rare religious portrait from the colonial Southwest; Thomas Jefferson's compilation of the Gospels; the sunstone on the original Mormon Temple in Nauvoo, Illinois.
